flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What execution model does LangGraph use internally, and what is a super-step?
flashcards.a: Pregel-style bulk-synchronous message passing (Google, 2010). A super-step is one tick: every scheduled node runs (possibly in parallel), all their writes are reduced into the channels, a checkpoint is written, then the next tick is scheduled from nodes with inbound messages. Halts when no node has inbound messages.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What is the default reducer for a state key, and what happens if two nodes write it in the same super-step?
flashcards.a: The default is LAST WRITE WINS (overwrite). Two writes in ONE super-step raise `InvalidUpdateError: At key 'k': Can receive only one value per step. Use an Annotated key to handle multiple values.` Two writes on CONSECUTIVE super-steps raise nothing and silently discard the first.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What is a reducer's signature, and why does `Annotated[list, operator.add]` exist?
flashcards.a: `(current, update) -> new`. It exists because a channel without a reducer accepts exactly one write per super-step, so any parallel fan-out or Send map-reduce writing a shared channel is broken by construction. It is the fan-in contract, not typing decoration.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.a: `operator.add` concatenates blindly. `add_messages` matches on message `id` and REPLACES an existing message with the same id, and coerces `{"role":..,"content":..}` dicts into LangChain message objects. The id-matching is why HITL edits and `update_state` correct a message instead of duplicating it.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: How do you bypass a reducer and set a channel directly?
flashcards.a: `Overwrite(value)` from `langgraph.types`, e.g. `return {"messages": Overwrite([summary])}`. Constraint: only one node may Overwrite a given key per super-step, otherwise `InvalidUpdateError`.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What is the default `recursion_limit` in current LangGraph, what did it used to be, and where does it go in config?
flashcards.a: 1000 super-steps as of langgraph 1.0.6; it was 25 for the framework's first two years. It is a TOP-LEVEL config key: `config={"recursion_limit": 40}`. Nested under `configurable` it is silently ignored. Exceeding it raises `GraphRecursionError`.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What does `Send` do, and how is it different from a conditional edge returning a list of node names?
flashcards.a: `Send(node, per_call_state)` runs the SAME node N times on N DIFFERENT states, returned as a list from a conditional edge. A conditional edge returning `["a","b"]` runs two DIFFERENT nodes on the SAME state. Send requires a reducer on the fan-in channel and a `max_concurrency` bound.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: Your fan-in node sees only some of the fan-out results and no error is raised. Cause and fix?
flashcards.a: Unequal branch lengths: the fan-in node's inbound edges were satisfied before the longer branch finished, so it ran on a partial channel. Fix: `add_node("synthesise", fn, defer=True)`, which delays it until all pending tasks complete. Symmetric test fixtures never trigger it.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: When do you use `Command` instead of a conditional edge, and what are the two gotchas?
flashcards.a: When you need to update state AND route in one decision: `Command(update=..., goto=...)`. Gotchas: (1) you must annotate the return type `-> Command[Literal["a","b"]]` or the runtime can't render the graph or know destinations; (2) `goto` ADDS a dynamic edge and does not override a static `add_edge`, so both destinations run. One routing mechanism per node.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What belongs in graph state, and where do dependencies and large blobs go instead?
flashcards.a: State is serialised into a checkpoint at every super-step, so keep it small and serialisable: ids, decisions, counters, messages. Dependencies (DB connections, model name, tenant id) go in runtime context via `context_schema` + `Runtime[Ctx]`, which is NOT checkpointed. Large blobs go in the `Store` or object storage with only the key in state.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: Name the seven LangGraph stream modes and which require a checkpointer.
flashcards.a: `values`, `updates`, `messages`, `custom`, `checkpoints`, `tasks`, `debug`. `checkpoints`, `tasks`, and `debug` require a checkpointer. `debug` = checkpoints + tasks + metadata.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What do `version="v2"` and `version="v3"` change about streaming?
flashcards.a: v1 (still default) changes shape by options: raw dict, `(mode,data)` tuples, `(ns,data)` for subgraphs, triples for both. `version="v2"` (needs >=1.1) makes every chunk a uniform `StreamPart` `{type, ns, data}` and makes `invoke` return a `GraphOutput` with `.value`/`.interrupts`. `version="v3"` on `stream_events` (1.2, beta) gives typed per-channel projections: `.messages`, `.values`, `.interrupts`, `.output`.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: Three subgraph persistence modes via `compile(checkpointer=...)` and their tradeoffs?
flashcards.a: `None` (per-invocation, default): interrupts YES, memory across calls NO, parallel calls safe YES. `True` (per-thread): memory YES, own checkpoint history so inner time travel works, but parallel calls to the SAME subgraph conflict on the namespace. `False` (stateless): plain function call, no interrupts, no durable execution.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: What are `RetryPolicy`'s defaults, and which exceptions does it deliberately NOT retry?
flashcards.a: `max_attempts=3`, `initial_interval=0.5s`, `backoff_factor=2.0`, `max_interval=128s`, `jitter=True`. Default `retry_on` retries any exception EXCEPT ValueError, TypeError, ArithmeticError, ImportError, LookupError, NameError, SyntaxError, RuntimeError, ReferenceError, StopIteration, StopAsyncIteration, OSError. For requests/httpx it retries 5xx only.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: In what fixed order do per-node timeout, retry policy, and error handler compose?
flashcards.a: timeout raises `NodeTimeoutError` -> the retry policy decides whether to retry -> only after retries are exhausted does `error_handler` run (receiving a typed `NodeError`, and it can return a `Command` for Saga compensation). `interrupt()` bypasses both retries and the error handler. Timeouts and error handlers require langgraph>=1.2 and are async-node-only.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: Honestly, what does the graph abstraction buy you over a 40-line agent loop?
flashcards.a: Exactly three things: a checkpoint boundary at every super-step (turning restart into resume, which matters because 0.85^10 ~= 20%), declared merge semantics for parallel writes via reducers, and an inspectable/streamable topology with per-node retry, timeout, and cache policies. For a simple model->tool->model loop it buys almost none of that and costs you a framework in the stack trace plus a migration every couple of quarters.

flashcards.topic: LangGraph I: StateGraph, Reducers, Conditional Edges, Send
flashcards.q: Which LangGraph versions introduced what, and when?
flashcards.a: 1.0.0 on 2025-10-20 (GA). 1.1.0 on 2026-03-10: `version="v2"` unified StreamPart streaming and typed invoke. 1.2.0 on 2026-05-12: per-node timeouts, node-level `error_handler`, graceful shutdown via `RunControl.request_drain()`, `DeltaChannel` (beta), and `version="v3"` event streaming.
